title: QBR Conversation Guide + Slide Sets (Growth & Enterprise)
content:
Purpose
Provide a compact, conversation-led QBR deck template set with speaker notes and a renewal-focused playbook. Two flavors included: Growth/Standard (fast, metrics-first) and Enterprise (deep-technical + executive narrative). This doc is a working master: use as the canonical draft for sales-aligned QBRs, post-call action items, and renewal play mapping.

Audience
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Solutions Engineers (SEs) who join enterprise QBRs
- Account Executives (AEs) for renewal coordination

How to use this pack
- Pick the appropriate flavor (Growth/Standard vs Enterprise) based on ARR and complexity.
- Populate slides with live dashboard links (see Links section) before sending pre-read.
- Send 3 business days before QBR with a 2-sentence agenda and pre-read links.

Pre-read checklist (send with calendar invite)
- 1 page: usage snapshot (last 90 days), key success metric trend, health score
- Links to support tickets affecting QBR (open > P3)
- Invoice/contract summary and upcoming renewal window
- One-sentence ask for the customer (e.g., product adoption target, renewed committed capacity)

QUICK DECISION: Which flavor?
- Growth/Standard: ARR < $75k or low-integration customers, 30–45 minute meeting, 8–10 slide deck.
- Enterprise: ARR >= $75k or customers with private deployments, on-prem/VPC, multiple internal stakeholders, 60–90 minute meeting, 12–16 slide deck, SE presence required.

Slide outlines (Growth / Standard) — ~30–45m
1) Title + Meeting Objectives (1 slide, 2 min)
   - Speaker note: Reconfirm objectives, meeting length, and decision owner for any asks.
2) One-line customer success story (1 slide, 2 min)
   - Speaker note: 1–2 bullets: what improved, headline metric. Keep it customer-focused.
3) Health snapshot (1 slide, 3 min)
   - Key fields: usage % QoQ, API latency (p50/p95), error rate, tokens consumption, incidents last 90d.
   - Color code: Green/Yellow/Red with short rationale.
4) Adoption & feature usage (2 slides, 5 min)
   - Top 3 features by token count, new integrations, notable churn signals.
5) Business impact & ROI (1 slide, 5 min)
   - Show estimated cost savings or revenue enablement tied to specific uses.
6) Roadmap highlights & product connect (1 slide, 5 min)
   - What’s landed that matters, and what’s next that could unlock more value.
7) Risk & support items / open asks (1 slide, 5 min)
   - List open tickets and blockers with owners.
8) Renewal health & proposal preview (1 slide, 5 min)
   - Current term end, recommended offer, escalation path.
9) Action plan & next steps (1 slide, 3 min)
   - Owner, deadline, success criteria.
10) Appendix & data links (1 slide, 2 min)

Speaker cadence: CSM leads; SE jumps in for technical/SLI discussion. AE involved only for renewal negotiation slides.

Slide outlines (Enterprise) — ~60–90m
1) Title + Executive objectives (1 slide, 3 min)
   - Confirm exec-level outcomes. Ask: Who signs renewal?
2) Customer executive story (1 slide, 5 min)
   - ROI headline + quote from internal stakeholder if available.
3) Strategic health dashboard (2 slides, 8 min)
   - Usage cohorts (by team/product line), latency & availability SLIs, SLO attainment, incident timeline, MTTR.
4) Technical architecture & deployment footprint (2 slides, 8 min)
   - Hosting mode (hosted/dedicated/private), network patterns, data residency, KMS/HSM notes.
5) Cost breakdown & efficiency levers (1 slide, 8 min)
   - Token cost, batching, caching, quantization recommendations tried or planned.
6) Quality & regressions (1 slide, 7 min)
   - Eval results, prompt sets, quality alerts since last QBR.
7) Compliance & audit highlights (1 slide, 5 min)
   - Logs retention, SOC/ISO/GDPR posture for their tenancy.
8) Support & SLAs (1 slide, 5 min)
   - Recent incidents, post mortem actions, runbook ownership.
9) Renewal options & commercial paths (2 slides, 10 min)
   - Base renewal, add-ons (dedicated pools, private controls), timeline and lost-revenue risk if delayed.
10) Negotiation ladder & decision calendar (1 slide, 5 min)
   - Suggested concessions, approval gates, exec sponsor asks.
11) Risk heatmap & mitigation plan (1 slide, 5 min)
   - Top 3 risks (tech, usage, budget) + mitigation owners.
12) Action plan, owners & date commitments (2 slides, 5–10 min)
13) Appendix: logs, evals, open tickets (2 slides)

Speaker notes: Use a story arc — "what changed" -> "why it matters" -> "what we recommend" -> "decisions we need today". For enterprise, prep an SE-run tech deep-dive and ensure a named exec sponsor is present.

Renewal playbook (compact)
- T-minus 90d: Trigger automated renewal health check (sheet update + risk tag). Outreach: CSM opens renewal thread in Slack and sets internal kickoff.
- T-minus 60d: Execute QBR (if scheduled) or dedicated renewal review. Provide pricing scenarios and contract summary.
- T-minus 30d: Confirm decision maker, procurement lead, and finance stakeholder. Send legal/PO checklist.
- T-minus 14d: Final commercial terms, draft MSA/contract redlines.
- T-minus 7d: Close — prepared PO, signed SOW, or agreed extension.

Renewal risk scoring (example)
- Score 0–10 (10 worst) derived from: usage decline, open P1/P2s, exec engagement (none=+3), product fit concerns, budget signals.
- Action: score >=6 -> AE + CS + Solutions Eng joint play, weekly standup.

Simple renewal tracker (paste into shared sheet)
Columns: Account | ARR | Renewal Date | Decision Maker | Renewal Score | Last 90d Usage % | Open P1/P2 | Recommended Offer | Next Action | Owner
Example rows:
ACME Corp | 180000 | 2026-08-15 | Maria Gomez (CTO) | 7 | -12% | 1P1 | Renew + dedicated pool | Schedule exec review | Priya Nair
Nimbus Labs | 32000 | 2026-05-02 | Ben Park (Head AI) | 3 | +18% | 0 | Standard renewal | Auto-renew email | CSM assigned

Ask ladder (how to structure asks in meeting)
- Level 0 (small): minor adoption commitment (increase token cap by 10%)
- Level 1 (medium): commit to 6-mo reserved capacity (saves X%)
- Level 2 (large): multi-year Dedicated/Private proposal + exec sponsor commitment

Email templates (short)
- Pre-read invite: "Hi {name}, attaching a short pre-read ahead of our QBR on {date}. Link includes usage snapshot, open tickets, and a proposed renewal preview. Main ask: confirm availability of {decision maker}. Thanks — Priya"
- Post-QBR action summary: "Thanks — agreed actions: 1) {owner} to deliver {item} by {date}. Renewal recommended offer: {offer}. Next meeting: {date}."

Operational play snippets (notes to CSM)
- If usage down > 15%: run a micro-adoption workshop within 7 days. Invite SE.
- If latency > p95 target: open priority triage with SRE and schedule architecture review.
- If exec sponsor unknown: escalate to AE and ask for intro within 5 business days.

Metrics & data sources (what to prepare)
- Product dashboard: tokens by endpoint, user cohorts, churned API keys
- Observability: per-route latency p50/p95, error budgets, incident timelines
- Billing sheet: invoice history, committed vs actual usage, discount schedule
- Support queue: open tickets w/owner and SLA breach risk

Risk color legend (use in slides)
- Green = operating within expected ranges; no active blockers
- Yellow = trending down or 1–2 operational items open; monitor and own
- Red = major outage, executive-level dissatisfaction, or contract-level risk

Appendix: sample data snippets to paste into slides
- 90d usage mini-table (copy into slide)
  Team | Avg tokens/day | % change vs prev 90d
  Search | 1.2M | +9%
  Chat | 420k | -14%
  Ingest | 80k | +2%

- Incident summary (last 6 months)
  Date | Severity | Brief | Owner | Status
  2025-09-11 | Sev2 | Token service latency spike during batch jobs | Eng-sre | Resolved

Recommended folder & filenames for final upload
- <account>-qbr-pre-read.pdf (1 page)
- <account>-qbr-deck-growth.pptx or <account>-qbr-deck-enterprise.pptx
- <account>-qbr-actions.csv (open action export)

Notes / open questions (working items)
- Do we publish a single standard pricing ladder for CSMs to reference? (action: ask RevOps)
- Should we require SE involvement for all renewals > $100k/yr? (action: sync with Eng-solutioning)
- Add a one-slide security posture export for all private deployments.

Next steps (internal)
- Marco: convert Enterprise outline into a slide master (due 2026-03-12).
- Lena: draft pre-read one-pager template and share in /CS/templates (due 2026-03-10).
- Priya: piloting with three accounts in March (Acme, Nimbus, Solace). Collect feedback and iterate.

End of doc
